title: Module with Submodules
story: Your game has grown: player systems, enemy AI, world generation, UI, sound. One module isn't enough — you need a nested module hierarchy. Submodules organize complex systems into a tree structure.
why: Submodules let you nest modules inside modules, creating a hierarchical organization that mirrors your application's logical structure.
analogy: A filing cabinet has drawers (modules), each drawer has folders (submodules), each folder has documents (functions and types). You don't dump everything in one drawer — you organize by category and subcategory. Submodules give you that filing cabinet structure.
try_it: Add a third submodule `staff` with `Teacher` type and `assign_course` function. Add re-exports in the parent `school` module so users can do `school.promote(...)` directly. Try accessing a private item in a submodule to see the visibility rules in action.
tips: Submodules must be marked `pub mod` to be visible outside the parent
Each submodule can have its own types, functions, constants
Re-exports from parent can flatten the hierarchy for consumers
common_mistakes: Creating too-deep hierarchies that become confusing — 2-3 levels is usually enough
Forgetting `pub` on submodule declarations — they're private by default too
Putting unrelated things in the same submodule just because they're small
